newsitem.title: JAPAN: Strong BOJ tankan rocks Japanese financial markets.
newsitem.headline: Strong BOJ tankan rocks Japanese financial markets.

text.p: A surprisingly strong improvement in business sentiment shown in the Bank of Japan's key "tankan" corporate survey rocked financial markets on Wednesday.

The dollar dipped more than one yen from late Tuesday New York levels after the release of the quarterly survey. Japanese government bond and euroyen futures tumbled on the improved economic picture, while Tokyo stocks put on handsome gains.

The closely watched diffusion index for major manufacturers in the June tankan was plus seven, up from plus two in March and well above economists' forecasts which ranged from minus four to plus four.
Non-manufacturers and smaller firms, however, remained significantly less optimistic, the tankan showed.
The index represents the percentage of companies which see business conditions as favourable minus the percentage of those viewing conditions as unfavourable.

The tankan results led some market participants to speculate that the BOJ could tighten its credit policy by this autumn. Others, however, said it was still too early to make conclusions about the timing of a credit tightening.

Taisuke Tanaka, global foreign exchange strategist at Credit Suisse First Boston in Tokyo, said he does not expect the tankan to result in an immediate change in the BOJ's monetary policy nor renewed strength in the value of the yen.

"The tankan showed a bi-polarisation of the Japanese economy. Big firms, mainly exporters, are reaping positive results from their restructuring efforts. Other firms, however, are falling behind," Tanaka said.

"We cannot count on exporters to be the locomotive for the Japanese economy as they are still in a restructuring process. Moreover, an export-led recovery would create a political problem for the United States and Japan," he said.
Tanaka expects the dollar to move within a range of 112-115 yen until more economic data is released.
"Whether the dollar will test levels above 115 yen again is likely to depend on the U.S. and Japanese economic indicators for this summer, especially consumption data," he said.
The dollar stood at 113.55/60 yen at midday, after falling as low as 113.35 yen earlier. It closed at 114.90/95 yen in New York on Tuesday.

The positive business outlook as reflected in the tankan also helped Tokyo stocks to rally. The Nikkei 225 stock average ended the morning up 243.03 points, or 1.19 percent, at 20,584.96, after rising as high as 20,669.47.
"The tankan nullified fears that Japan's economy was lagging, providing investors with confidence to buy," said Nomura Securities general manager Takahisa Matsuura.
But it had the opposite effect on the bond market, sending the key September Japanese government bond (JGB) futures down 1.31 at 123.10 by midday.

"Following the strong tankan, the bond market's overly pessimistic view of the economy is starting to be corrected. But it may take a while before the market sees a rise in interest rates," said Tadao Sakashima, assistant general manager of the bond department at Daiwa Securities Co.
"The long-end of the JGB yield curve, therefore, may move within a range of between 2.7 and 2.9 percent until autumn."
Euroyen futures were also severely hit by the tankan. The benchmark March futures contract was down 0.19 at 98.75 at midday, after falling as low as 98.73.
Shin Nagai, vice president at ABN-Amro Bank's Treasury Department said: "The yen debt yield curve is likely to steepen as the market tries to reassess the economy under a more positive light."
The debt market will again try to absorb the fact that the Japanese economy is on a recovery track led by exports, and push the longer-end yields higher, he added.

Meanwhile, the BOJ is likely to continue holding down short-term interest rates as the tankan and other recent economic data failed to offer a determinant factor to justify a credit tightening, Nagai said.
